title: Rising river near a community centre
audience: Volunteer coordinator or junior responder on duty
context: Educational, non-combat civil-protection scenario. No weapons, harm or combat content.

steps.title: A flood warning
steps.situation: 16:10. An official flood warning is issued for the river next to the community centre where you are the volunteer coordinator on duty. Water is expected in the street within about two hours. Eight people are in the building, and two of them need help to walk.
steps.question: What is your first instruction?

options.text: Wait and watch the river to see whether the water really rises.
Tell everyone to go home on their own by whichever route they prefer.
Gather the group and the grab bag, check first on the two people who need help, and start moving to the meeting point on higher ground.

steps.why: Acting on the warning, helping those who need support and moving before the water arrives keeps the group safe.
steps.hint: A warning means flooding is expected. Think about the people who need help to move, and the time you have.

steps.title: The street is under water
steps.situation: At the end of the street the road is covered by brown water about knee-deep, and you can see it moving. The meeting point is 200 metres away across the water. A path over the hill is dry but adds about ten minutes.
steps.question: How do you get the group to the meeting point?

options.text: Cross in a line, holding hands, because the water looks shallow.
Load everyone into the minibus and drive through the water.
Take the longer path over the hill that stays above the water.

steps.why: A longer route that stays dry is safer than a shorter one through floodwater.
steps.hint: Floodwater hides its depth and its force. Think about which route stays dry, even if it is longer.

steps.title: Back at the building
steps.situation: The next morning the water has dropped. The group wants to return to collect belongings. The ground floor is wet, the lights flicker, and the authorities have not yet said the area is safe.
steps.question: What do you do?

options.text: Do not go in. Wait for the official all-clear, keep away from electrical equipment, and report the building so the electrics can be checked.
Go in and switch on the lights to see how bad the damage is.
Start pumping out the flooded basement as fast as possible.

steps.why: Entering before the area is declared safe, or touching wet electrics, is dangerous. The electrics must be checked first.
steps.hint: Think about what may still be unsafe inside after a flood, and who decides when it is safe.
